name: empty-dns-permitted-allows-anything-valid
description: An empty-IA5String dNSName permitted subtree is treated as 'matches any DNS name' by NSS-lineage validators. RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 does not normatively specify what an empty constraint base means; the convention reads section 4.2.1.10 strictly ('any DNS name that can be constructed by simply adding zero or more labels to the left-hand side of the name satisfies the name constraint') and notes that adding labels to the empty string yields every name.
references: Go name_constraints_test "empty DNS permitted constraint allows anything"
notes: All three of OpenSSL (since the original 2008 commit), Go (which cites NSS in its pre-2025 comment), and GnuTLS reach the 'valid' verdict for this case, by deliberate code paths.
OpenSSL: nc_dns short-circuits 'Empty matches everything' so the leaf's DNS SAN is treated as inside the permitted subtree.
Go: newDNSConstraints sees a zero-length entry and sets dnsConstraints.all = true, short-circuiting the query.
GnuTLS: check_dns_constraints explicitly skips empty permitted entries (treating them as 'not a permit'); when no other permit exists, the chain falls through to accept.
